scenario_summary: Customer is seeking a refund for a service subscription canceled 34 days ago, which is outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is DeShawn Jefferson and I'm 65. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello, Mr. Jefferson. I understand how frustrating it can be to return from travel and find an unexpected charge. I would be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide your account number and the email address associated with your subscription?
Sure, my account number is 8849201 and my email is d.jefferson@email.com.
Thank you for that information. For security, could you please confirm the last four digits of the payment method on file?

Thank you, Mr. Jefferson. I have verified your account details. I see the subscription was indeed canceled 34 days ago. While our 'Terms of Service Section 4.2' strictly limits automated refunds to 30 days, I can see this is your first cancellation request in over two years. Given your long-standing history with us, I am authorized to make a one-time exception to our policy.
Oh, that would be wonderful. I really appreciate you taking the time to look into my history.

It is my pleasure. I have processed the refund for the $49.99 charge to your original payment method. You should see the credit appear in your bank statement within 3 to 5 business days. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?

resolution_summary: The agent verified the account and, noting the customer's long-standing account history, applied a one-time exception to the standard 30-day refund policy to process the requested refund.
